At work, I noticed that people often had their own ways of doing the same things on a computer. Some methods were outdated. Others were inefficient or simply different. Often there was a better way, but that knowledge stayed with the person who had discovered it.

That's why I built Zipr: a toolbox anyone can use to turn the way they work into a single button press. It saves time, cuts out repetitive tasks, and makes it easy to share useful shortcuts with friends and colleagues.

Why is the app free if the team version isn't?
Because the app is complete on its own: it stores and runs everything on your machine, so it would keep working whatever we did. Sharing needs a server, and that is the part you pay for.

The free app is the trial — the same build a paying team runs, with no time limit. There's no separate trial of the shared version, because setting one up is the paid work itself. Talk to us and we'll work out a sensible pilot.
Do I need to understand commands or code?

No. Start by describing the task in your own words. Zap proposes the steps and shows their settings so you can review them. Some shortcuts involve commands or configuration, so inspect those carefully before running them.
Can Zap run commands on my computer without asking?

Zap itself cannot press Test or run the shortcut. When you choose to test or run a shortcut, its configured steps execute. Review commands and permissions, and add confirmation steps when appropriate.
What happens if we stop paying?

Nothing is deleted or held hostage. Reading keeps working, changes are refused, and you can export everything at any point without settling anything first. Self-hosted licences warn you for a month before they expire. Everything on individual machines is unaffected.

Does Zap create a finished shortcut automatically?
Zap creates and edits a draft. You review it, test it yourself and save it when you're satisfied. A draft is not the same thing as a verified result.
Does a successful test prove the task worked?

Not necessarily. Zipr starts a command without waiting for it to finish, so a test may show that the command started without proving its final result. Check the output and the actual outcome when a task matters.
What happens when I save a shortcut?
It becomes an ordinary personal shortcut, without a link back to the Zap conversation. You can edit, run or share it like other shortcuts you've created.

Zap supports Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, including compatible models hosted locally. The model must support tool calling, and Zipr checks compatibility when you connect it.
Where is my API key stored?
Your key is stored in your operating system's keychain. On Linux, where Zipr does not use a system keychain for this purpose, Zap works through a team server rather than a personal API key.

Yes. On organisation-managed computers, an administrator can leave the choice to the user, require the team server, or turn Zap off. Turning it off preserves drafts already in progress but prevents new conversations.
Does Zap keep a record of my conversation?
Drafts are stored on your computer until you save or discard them. The app does not log prompts or replies. The information sent to your chosen model is described in the data section above.

OpenAI only supports tool calling for this model through its Responses API. Zipr uses Chat Completions, so Check and save refuses it.

Managing billing for ChatGPT and the API platform
Check and save says the provider refused the request (401)
The key wasn't accepted. Check it was copied whole, with nothing before or after it, and that it hasn't been deleted or expired at the provider. If in doubt, create a new key and paste that.
It says the provider refused the request because of credit, quota or billing
The account has no credit left, or no payment method. Add credit in the provider's billing settings, wait a minute, and press Check and save again.
It says the model answered without calling a tool
Zap needs a model that can call tools, and checks for it before saving. Use one of the models listed for your provider on this page, typed exactly as shown.
It says the model doesn't exist, or wasn't found

Model names must be typed exactly, in lower case, with the hyphens. Copy one from this page. Providers also retire models over time; if a listed one has gone, the provider's models page names its replacement.
It says this computer has no keychain
Linux has no system keychain, and Zipr won't write a key to disk. On Linux, use Zap through your organisation's Zipr server instead of a personal key.
Set a monthly spending limit at the provider, so a busy month can't surprise you.

Hosted or self-hosted — which should we pick?

It is the same software, so choose on operations. Hosted: we run, patch and back it up, and you pay per person. Self-hosted: your data never leaves your infrastructure, it can run with no internet, and you pay per deployment. Teams with a platform group and a data-residency policy usually self-host; everyone else is better served hosted.

On the hosted service, anyone an administrator adds to your organisation — from the moment they are added, whether or not they sign in. Remove them and they stop counting at the next renewal. Self-hosting doesn't count people at all.
Can we start hosted and move to our own servers later?

Yes — your content exports as one file whenever you want it. There is no one-click conversion that carries accounts and history across yet, so plan the move as a piece of work, and tell us early so we can help.
By invoice. Hosted is billed yearly or monthly per person; self-hosted is an annual figure for the deployment. Either way you get a quote before anything starts.

Self-hosted, it never leaves your infrastructure and we have no copy. Hosted, it sits in a database belonging to your organisation alone — we operate it, so access is governed by contract and policy.

Your data is never held hostage
Export everything as one file at any time. If a licence or invoice lapses, reading keeps working while changes are refused.

Self-hosted, on the server you run it on, and we hold nothing. Hosted, in a database provisioned for your organisation alone, so it can be backed up and restored on its own. Either way, each machine also keeps a copy so the app is fast and works offline.
What does the app send over the network?
Only your teams' shortcuts and the sign-in that authorises them, and only to the deployment it is pointed at. With no deployment configured, it makes no network requests at all.
Can we run it somewhere with no internet access?
Yes, self-hosted. The licence verifies offline, so air-gapped is a supported configuration, not a workaround — and we'll help you set it up. The hosted service can't be air-gapped.

In your browser — the app opens the sign-in page and never handles your Zipr password itself. Google, Microsoft Entra and Okta are supported, so people join and leave wherever you already manage that.
What happens to our data if we stop paying?

Reading keeps working while changes are refused, and you can export everything at any point without settling anything first. Hosted, the data is kept for the period set out in your agreement after suspension before anything is removed. Self-hosted, it is on your own disk and we can't touch it; the licence warns you for a month before it expires.
Your administrators decide, per team. The system won't confirm that something exists just because someone guessed its address.
How do we get security updates?
New versions are published on the downloads page and you roll them out on your own schedule. Nothing updates itself underneath you.
